summary0: There is no sign-up, and the content you create in the Apps stays on your device. The only things the Apps send to us are anonymous usage statistics (Section 7) and, from Windows apps, a purchase record when a PRO purchase completes (Section 6).
principle: You can use the Apps without creating an account or signing in. The data the Apps handle — clipboard items, notes, timers, photos, settings and so on — is stored and processed on your device by default and is never sent to us. The exceptions are optional features you turn on yourself (Section 3), the outside services the Apps rely on (Sections 4–6) and anonymous usage statistics (Section 7), all described below. Information is sent to our server only in two cases: anonymous usage statistics (Section 7) and the purchase record from Windows apps (Section 6).
usage_html:
From the updates released in November 2026 onward, our Android and Windows apps send anonymous usage statistics to our server, so we can see where new users get stuck and whether our changes help.

  • What is sent. A random ID the app creates the first time it opens (it is not linked to your account, advertising ID or device, and reinstalling the app creates a new one), the app's name and version, your operating system version, your device's language and country settings, whether PRO is active, and simple events with the number of days since installation — for example that the app was opened, onboarding was finished, a permission was granted, the main feature was used (as a count), a PRO screen or an ad was shown, or a purchase was made.
  • What is never sent. Anything you create or handle in the Apps (clipboard items, notes, photos, web addresses, calculations, the apps you choose and so on), your name, email address, advertising ID or account.
  • Users in Europe. If your device's SIM, mobile network or region setting is in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom or Switzerland, the apps collect and send nothing.
  • Where it is kept and for how long. On Google Cloud (Cloud Run in Tokyo, Japan, and Firestore in Seoul, South Korea). We do not keep IP addresses with this data, do not share it with anyone, and use it only to improve the Apps. It is deleted automatically after 13 months.
  • Stopping it. Uninstalling an app stops its statistics and deletes its random ID.
history: • 2026-11-11 Added anonymous usage statistics sent by our Android and Windows apps (Section 7) and updated the core principle and summary to match. Later sections were renumbered.
